education_lens: Scholars recognize the Old Kiln script on the seawall; dockworkers only know the pier names.
lifespan_lens: Humans treat the Cinder War as grandfathers' tales; local stone-dwarves still hold grudges from it.

local_sayings.detail: 'Keep your boots dry and your wick lit'—used both as a farewell and a warning against cutting corners.
local_sayings.hook: Merchants distrust anyone who replies without tapping their belt lantern.

regional_superstitions.detail: Never whistle on the outer pier after dusk; locals swear the tide-hounds follow the tune.

seasonal_festivals.detail: Night of First Embers—lantern boats launched onto the bay each autumn.
seasonal_festivals.hook: Pickpockets and smugglers use the smoke cover.

famous_monuments.detail: Twin basalt lighthouse pillars jutting half-collapsed out of the harbor mouth.
famous_monuments.hook: Low tide exposes an interior spiral stair.

scarred_landscapes.detail: The Glass Flats north of town where wildfire and kiln-blast fused the beach sand.
scarred_landscapes.hook: Scavengers harvest sharp obsidian shards at dawn.

rival_families.detail: House Vane and House Corrin dispute ownership of the east salt-drying piers.
rival_families.hook: Both secretly hire outsiders to sabotage the other's drying racks.

local_heroes.detail: Old Mara, the ferrywoman who rowed thirty children through a burning squall.

famous_orders.detail: Out of scope for this small fishing harbor.
